unit_title: Health Literacy and Decision Making in High School
standards: Michigan HESG 2025 Grades 9-12 [12.1.PHW] Personal Health and Wellness — Self-Awareness and Analyzing Influences
Michigan HESG 2025 Grades 9-12 [12.3.PHW] Personal Health and Wellness — Information and Resource Seeking
Michigan HESG 2025 Grades 9-12 [12.4.PHW] Personal Health and Wellness — Decision Making and Problem Solving

prompts.prompt: Explain what health literacy means at the high-school level in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of internal and external influences on a health decision.
Apply source quality: authorship, evidence, currency, and conflict of interest in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving a repeatable decision process for health choices; correct it and explain why.
Connect short-term convenience versus longer-term consequence with reviewing a decision after the fact without self-blame. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Work a fictional high-school health decision end to end: name the influences, evaluate two competing sources, run the decision process, and state what evidence would change the decision. The learner never has to use a real decision from their own life.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence and reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check on a later occasion.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source on one occasion, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
privacy_note: All scenarios are fictional. The learner is never asked to describe a real health decision, condition, or family situation.

Connect vehicle, water, fire, and home-hazard prevention with bystander responsibility and safe intervention limits. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

unit_title: Fueling, Movement, Sleep, and Recovery Without Diet Culture

Michigan HESG 2025 Grades 9-12 [12.1.BEPA] Balanced Eating and Physical Activity — Self-Awareness and Analyzing Influences

prompts.prompt: Explain adequate fueling for growth, school load, and activity in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of hydration across a day.
Apply sleep need, sleep debt, and circadian timing in high school in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving recovery after effort, illness, or a heavy week; correct it and explain why.

Connect evaluating supplement, energy-product, and fitness-industry claims with body respect and resisting appearance-based health messaging. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Evaluate three fictional wellness plans for adequacy, safety, evidence, flexibility, and cost, then revise the weakest one. No calorie counts, weights, body-size targets, diet rules, or good/bad food labels are used or produced.

Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of how communicable conditions transmit and how transmission is interrupted.
Apply HIV: accurate transmission and non-transmission facts, testing, and treatment as prevention in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
